subject: general
question: Rohit bought an article for ₹4,400. He spent ₹3,600 on it. He marked the price 25% above his total cost price. He then allowed two successive discounts of 19% on it. Find the selling price (in ₹) of the article.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Cost Price (CP) = 4,400 + 3,600 = 8,000.

Marked Price (MP) = 8,000 × 125/100 = 10,000.

Selling Price (SP) = 10,000 × (81/100) × (81/100).

SP = 10,000 × 6,561/10,000 = 6,561.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹6,561.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Purchase Price = 4,400, Overhead Expenses = 3,600, Markup % = 25%, Successive Discounts = 19% each.

**Formulas:** Total CP = Purchase Price + Overheads | MP = CP × (100 + Markup%)/100 | SP = MP × (100 − D₁%)/100 × (100 − D₂%)/100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b08f652a984baaa92983ea97fd176a5dc82f6c048a5801c0daa605c67df341fc.png] 

⇒ **Total Cost Price (CP)** = 4,400 + 3,600 = 8,000

⇒ **Marked Price (MP)** = 8,000 + (25% of 8,000) = 8,000 + 2,000 = 10,000

⇒ **First Discounted Price** = 10,000 − (19% of 10,000) = 10,000 − 1,900 = 8,100

⇒ **Final Selling Price (SP)** = 8,100 − (19% of 8,100) = 8,100 − 1,539 = 6,561

**∴ The correct answer is ₹6,561.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Cost Price Calculation

When a person spends money on repairs, transportation, or overheads, these costs are added to the initial purchase price to get the **Effective Cost Price**.

Successive Discount Formula

Single equivalent discount for two successive discounts a% and b% = (a + b − ab/100)%. Here: 19 + 19 − (19×19)/100 = 38 − 3.61 = 34.39%.
